emma: FYI during today's onboarding workshop I hit a weird parity problem between the Next starter (edge+server components) and the Python LlamaIndex sample. JS starter double-indexes some docs only when run from the browser SSR path, but node/server-only runs are fine.

raj: interesting. so behavior differs between edge/SSR vs node server? can you sketch the topology?

emma: yes. Next starter uses an edge API route that proxies to the SDK; the same indexer is also invoked from a server-worker background job for larger uploads. Dupes only show up when the initial call comes from the edge handler + the background job concurrently picks up the same doc. logs: 
```
2026-08-11T11:00:01.001Z edge-handler received index request id=up-17
2026-08-11T11:00:01.002Z sdk edge auth refresh ok
2026-08-11T11:00:01.003Z edge-handler sent embedding request for doc=up-17
2026-08-11T11:00:01.004Z background-worker started upload id=up-17
2026-08-11T11:00:01.005Z backend embed accepted for id=up-17
2026-08-11T11:00:01.006Z edge-handler observed no immediate ack, retried -> backend embed accepted for id=up-17 (duplicate)
```

emma: note the edge SDK runtime uses fetch() and the runtime occasionally returns a network error for streamed responses which the SDK treats as a retry. background-worker is node and doesn't retry in the same way.

sam: that’s a new twist — cross-runtime retry semantics + concurrent systems. previous threads were mostly single-runtime races.

aditya: do we have a consistent idempotency story across runtimes? header semantics are straightforward, but browser contexts can't reliably persist long-lived keys across tabs/instances.

mira: workaround idea for starter: generate a deterministic idempotency key from content + source URL (e.g., sha256(docText + sourceUrl)) and attach `x-redwood-idempotency` for all index calls. That key is deterministic so background job and edge call will collide server-side and dedupe.

emma: I like deterministic keys, but UX: users may not know to include sourceUrl or may upload same doc with slight whitespace changes. Also hashing in browser needs a small lib; we can provide `redwood/embeds.hashKey(doc)` helper in the starter.

aditya: SDK thought: add an `embed.coalesce()` helper exported by `@redwood/inference-js` that accepts `{ input, key?: string }` and will use a best-effort in-memory coalesce in runtime + emit deterministic `x-redwood-idempotency` header if key not supplied (uses content hash). On server runtimes it can persist a very short TTL lock in-memory; on edge runtimes with no shared state it will still emit deterministic header so server-side dedupe kicks in. Feature-flagged behind `REDWOOD_SDK_COALESCE=on`.

sam: love that. two benefits: (1) a simple developer ergonomics helper so starters don't have to implement their own dedupe, (2) consistent cross-runtime behavior via deterministic idempotency header.

mira: quick docs note: show recommended pattern: `await client.embeddings.coalesce({ input: doc.text, source: doc.url })` and explain tradeoffs (deterministic vs random keys).

emma: edge-case: if users intentionally re-upload slightly modified doc we don't want accidental dedupe. we should document that idempotency key must include a version or timestamp when they want a new embedding.

aditya: agreed. also SDK will expose `coalesce({ forceNew: true })` for explicit bypass. Server-side we'll add a 5-second dedupe window for identical keys. Longer dedupe windows to be an opt-in server config.

raj: tests? can we mock both edge and background worker in CI to ensure no duplicates?

sam: I'll add a small integration test in the starter that spawns two concurrent index calls (one mimicking edge fetch, one node) against a mocked embed endpoint and assert backend sees only 1 embed per key. I'll also add an eval smoke that checks token usage <1.1x baseline.

emma: timeline: I can add a tiny helper in the starter that computes the key and swaps internal calls to `client.embeddings.coalesce`. I'll also add a note in quickstart about including `source` or `version` in the key for intentional reindexing.

aditya: I'll work on SDK PR: export `embeddings.coalesce`, implement deterministic hashing, wire `x-redwood-idempotency` header when present, and add `REDWOOD_SDK_COALESCE` flag. Server-side ticket to dedupe identical keys within 5s is filed (#4332).

mira: docs will add examples for Next edge, SSR, and background workers showing how to use `coalesce` and when to set `forceNew: true`.

ci-bot: ci/starter-integration job queued -> will run once PRs are opened

sam: small follow-up: add a note for LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors to surface `coalesce` usage in their adapter examples. Some connectors have internal batching that may need to pass `key` through.

aditya: yep — will add an adapter shim `redwood-langchain` example showing `await coalesce({ input, key: hash(input + source) })` inside the run step.

emma: thanks all. once PRs land let's run the workshop flow end-to-end and confirm the cost/eval harness metrics improve. I'll mark this thread resolved after green CI. :thumbsup:
